div.l: Ne of his knobbys syttyng on his chekys
Well loued he oynons garlyk ⁊and lekys
And for to drynk strong wyn as red as blood
Then wolde he speke ⁊and crye as he were wood
And whan he had well dronk the wyn
Then wolde he speke no worde but latyn
A fewe termes had he two or thre
That he had lerned of som man of decree
No wonder is he herde it all the day
And also ye knowe well that a Iay
Can calle watte as well as can the pope
But who cowde hym in other thynges grope
Then had he spent all his phylosophye
Ay questio quid queris wolde he crye
He was a gentyll harlot and a kynde
A better felowe sholde men not fynde
He wolde suffre for a quart of wyn
A good felowe to haue his concubyn
A twelne monthe ⁊and excuse hym at the fulle
Full pryuely a fynche also cowde he pulle
And yf he founde o wher a good felawe
He wolde teche hym anon to haue awe
In suche caas as the arched ekenes crs
But yf mannys soule were in his purs
For in his purs he sholde punysshed be
Purs is the archedekenes helle sayd he
But well I wote he lyed ryght in dede
Of cursyng ought eche man to drede
For cursyng woll sle ryght as soyllyng saueth
And also ware hym of a significauit
In daunger had he at his owne gyse
All the yonge gyrles of the dyocyse
And knewe of ther coıı̄unsell ⁊and was of ther rede
A garlonde he had set vpon his hede
As grete as it were an alestake
A bokeler had he made hym of a cake
Wyth hym there rode a gentyll pardoner
Of rouncyuale his frende ⁊and his comper
That streyȝt was come fro the court of rome
Full lowde he songe come hyther loue to me
